tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.our_fair: Guardians 53.6% / Rays 46.4% (devigged Pinnacle h2h, power devig); total 6.5: Over 52.0% / Under 48.0%
games.take: The ALCS shifts to Cleveland tied 1-1, and MLB moved this one up to 1pm ET to dodge the rain coming later in the day — an outdoor October game in Ohio with weather in the forecast is its own kind of volatility. It's a pitcher's duel on paper: Gavin Williams (1-0, 1.54 ERA this postseason, 24 Ks in 11.2 IP) for Cleveland against Griffin Jax for the Rays, who stole Game 2 behind Freddy Peralta's gem and a José Ramírez error. The market has this priced right — our fair line sits within a point of the board on every number. The angle here is the pitching and the weather, not the price.
games.title: ALCS Game 3
games.verdict: LEAN: Guardians -120 — no true edge (fair 53.6% vs 54.5% implied, -1.3% EV), but the lean is the home favorite: the better postseason arm in Williams, the crowd, and the game moved up so the weather shouldn't touch it. This is an opinion, not a play.

games.our_fair: Dodgers 58.6% / Brewers 41.4% (devigged Pinnacle h2h, power devig); total 7.5: Over 50.8% / Under 49.2%
games.take: Milwaukee is one win from its first World Series since 1982 (as an AL club) after last night's 6-2 Game 3 win — back-to-back seventh-inning homers off Blake Snell broke the Dodgers' 18-game postseason streak of winning when leading after six. The two-time defending champs have scored seven runs in three games and moved Shohei Ohtani to sixth in the order. Tonight: Tyler Glasnow (5-2, 3.53 ERA) for LA against a Brewers starter still TBA — Milwaukee's bullpen has been the story all October, and the Dodgers' offense is ice cold. The market is fair on the number, so this is a narrative game: desperation vs. destiny.
games.title: NLCS Game 4
games.verdict: LEAN: Dodgers -147 — no true edge (fair 58.6% vs 59.5% implied, -1.2% EV), but the lean is LA: elimination game, Glasnow on the mound, and a lineup that can't stay this cold forever. This is an opinion, not a play.

games.our_fair: Seahawks 57.0% / Broncos 43.0% (devigged Pinnacle h2h, power devig); spread Seahawks -2.5: 50.2%; total 40.5: Over 51.2% / Under 48.8%
games.take: The defending champs visit Mile High on a short week, both teams 3-2. The story is the injury report: Denver is without Pat Surtain II (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) in the secondary, with Riley Moss (ribs) questionable — while Seattle gets Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Leonard Williams back despite ankle issues. JSN has four 100-yard games in five weeks and seven receiving touchdowns; against a Surtain-less secondary, that's the matchup of the night. The line moved from Seahawks -1.5 to -2.5/-3 during the week as the injuries priced in, so the market caught up — our fair says this is priced right. Cold one in Denver (~50°F, rain tapering off), nothing severe.
games.title: Thursday Night Football — Week 6
games.venue: Empower Field at Mile High, Denver (outdoor)
games.verdict: LEAN: Seahawks -2.5 — no true edge (fair 50.2% vs 51.2% implied on the spread), but the lean is Seattle: the JSN matchup against a depleted secondary is the best unit edge on the field. This is an opinion, not a play.

games.our_fair: ECU 64.8% / UAB 35.2% (devigged Pinnacle h2h, power devig); spread ECU -5 covers 49.3%; total 47.5: Over 49.8% / Under 50.2%
games.take: Thursday's early window at Protective Stadium. East Carolina is laying five on the road, and the market's number matches our fair line almost exactly — no edge to bet either way. Both teams are mid-pack in the American, and the short week favors the team with the cleaner operation. When the number is this fair, the game is about watching, not betting.
games.title: East Carolina @ UAB
games.verdict: LEAN: East Carolina -5 — no true edge per our fair line (ECU -5 covers 49.3% vs 50.9% implied), but the lean is the road favorite: the better team laying a fair number. This is an opinion, not a play.

games.matchup: Georgia Southern Eagles @ Old Dominion Monarchs
games.our_fair: GASO 61.5% / ODU 38.5% (devigged Pinnacle h2h, power devig); spread GASO -3.5 covers 49.5%; total 46.5: Over 50.8% / Under 49.2%
games.take: Sun Belt Thursday night in Norfolk. Georgia Southern is a short road favorite, and the number is fair — our fair line has the spread at essentially a coin flip on the cover, so there's nothing to bet. These midweek Sun Belt games live on turnovers and special teams chaos; as a free opinion, take the team laying the fair number, but the honest call is that the market got this one right.
games.title: Georgia Southern @ Old Dominion
games.verdict: LEAN: Georgia Southern -3.5 — no true edge per our fair line (GASO -3.5 covers 49.5% vs 51.0% implied), but the lean is the Eagles: the better side of a fairly-priced short spread. This is an opinion, not a play.

games.market: Total 69.5 (Over -105 at multiple books; Pinnacle Over -119 / Under +102)
games.matchup: Colorado State Rams @ Texas State Bobcats
games.our_fair: Total 69.5: Over 52.5% / Under 47.5% (devigged Pinnacle, power devig); Texas State -14 covers 52.0%; TXST wins 84.8%
games.take: The nightcap in San Marcos and our one board play. Pinnacle's total is 69.5 with the Over at -119, but several books are still hanging Over 69.5 at -105 — that's a stale number against a 52.5% fair line, a +2.5% edge. The 'why': Texas State's tempo at home in this building has produced track meets, and Colorado State's defense hasn't shown it can get stops against this kind of pace. The Pinnacle market is 17 cents wide, so the number is real and liquid. Weather screen clean: no NWS alerts for San Marcos, ~84°F and dry at kickoff — nothing to slow the scoring.
games.title: Colorado State @ Texas State
games.verdict: LEAN: Over 69.5 — board play (+2.5% vs our fair on the stale -105). The fair total says the Over, the books are slow, and the matchup supports points. This one goes on the card.
